title: Exploring Dimensionality of the Workers’ Interest Scale in Engineering With Latiné Engineers
abstract: This study investigated the dimensionality of the Workers’ Interest Scale in Engineering (WISE) using data from 523 Latiné engineers. Exploratory graph analysis (EGA) was conducted to identify the underlying structure of the WISE, followed by bootstrap analysis to test item and dimension stability. We examined the conceptual alignment and statistical model fit of the dimensions. Group differences across gender and engineering disciplines were also assessed. Findings indicate that the final 39-item WISE captures five distinct dimensions of engineering interests: Technology and Engineering Innovation, Teamwork and Leadership, Research and Experimentation, Business Development, and Project Management. The final WISE items demonstrated high item stability, meaningful conceptual alignment, and good model fit. Moreover, group comparisons revealed variations in interests across gender groups (Cohen’s d ranged between .53 and .86) and engineering disciplines ( η 2 ranged between .01 and .16). Implications, limitations, and directions for future research are discussed.
